page_title: R2Drop — Native macOS Uploader for Cloudflare R2 by Paul Pierre

summary.name: R2Drop
summary.one_liner: R2Drop is a free, open-source native macOS menu bar app and CLI for uploading files and folders to Cloudflare R2 storage.
use_cases: Uploading files to Cloudflare R2 from Finder
Getting a public URL for a shared file automatically
Scripting R2 uploads from the terminal or CI
Switching between multiple Cloudflare accounts and buckets
Uploading large files or folders in parallel
summary.what_it_does: R2Drop is a native macOS menu bar app for uploading files to Cloudflare R2. Uploads can be started by right-clicking in Finder, dragging to the menu bar, or using the companion CLI, which shares the same config and queue as the app. After each upload, the public URL (including custom domain support) is copied to the clipboard. It supports multiple Cloudflare accounts with different buckets and path prefixes, switchable from the menu bar. Large files use multipart uploads in parallel chunks across up to 16 streams, and uploads are resumable. Credentials are stored in macOS Keychain, and files go directly from the Mac to R2 without a R2Drop server in between.
notable: Finder right-click, menu bar drag, and CLI upload methods sharing one config and queue
Public URL auto-copied to clipboard after upload, with custom domain support
Credentials stored only in macOS Keychain; no R2Drop server in the data path
Free and open source under the MIT license
caveats: Requires a Cloudflare account with R2 enabled and an R2-scoped API token; you pay Cloudflare for R2 storage beyond the free tier
Sends anonymous usage telemetry by default (can be turned off in Settings)
